articles.headline: Warriors star Stephen Curry leads Golden State to dominant OT win over Magic
keyFacts: Stephen Curry scored 41 points to lead the Golden State Warriors to a 126-119 overtime victory over the Orlando Magic on Saturday night.
The victory extended the Warriors' winning streak to seven games and set an NBA record for the most 40-point games by a player aged 35 or older.
The Warriors will attempt to extend their winning streak to eight games against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday.
body: Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Warriors star Stephen Curry leads Golden State to dominant OT win over Magic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors just keep finding ways to win. The Warriors outlasted the Orlando Magic 126-119 in overtime on Saturday night at Chase Center, as Curry delivered yet another vintage performance to extend the team’s winning streak to seven games .

The two-time MVP was simply unstoppable , finishing with 41 points on a blistering 13-of-19 shooting from the field. He knocked down five of his 10 3-point attempts and went a perfect 10-of-10 from the free-throw line, while also adding six rebounds and six assists.
The performance also put Curry in the record books . He now has the most 40-point games by a player 35 years or older in NBA history.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The superstar guard came through when the Warriors needed him most. With Golden State clinging to a 120-118 lead in the final minute of overtime, Curry was still going at the Magic defense, having already reached the 41-point mark, as Golden State pulled away for the win.

It was the latest in a string of big nights for Curry during the streak. He dropped 34 points against the Phoenix Suns last Monday and followed that up with 29 points in just 28 minutes in Thursday’s blowout win over the Miami Heat .

Curry had plenty of help against Orlando, too. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg continued his impressive start with 23 points on 9-of-15 shooting, along with eight rebounds and three blocks. Brandin Podziemski chipped in 15 points and seven rebounds, knocking down four of his five 3-point attempts, while Draymond Green orchestrated the offense with 13 assists.
As a team, the Warriors shot 53.8% from the field and 46.9% from deep, and they dished out 32 assists.

The Magic made the Warriors work for it. Franz Wagner led Orlando with 30 points and 11 assists, while Wendell Carter Jr. posted 19 points and 11 rebounds . Tristan da Silva added 19 points, and Anthony Black and Jamal Cain each scored 18.
Orlando also dominated the offensive glass with 24 offensive rebounds, but its 38.1% shooting from the field proved costly.
The win improved Golden State to 7-3 on the season, a remarkable turnaround after the team opened the year with three straight losses . Since then, the Warriors have not lost a game.
Curry and the Warriors will look to make it eight in a row when they close out their homestand against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday.
Related: Bill Simmons boldly declares Warriors star Stephen Curry is ‘so so back’ after OT win over Magic

articles.headline: James Talarico crashes ‘SNL’ cold open days after turning Texas blue
keyFacts: Newly elected Democratic Senator James Talarico appeared in a Saturday Night Live cold open sketch following his election victory.
Talarico won the Texas Senate race against Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton with just over 55 percent of the vote.
During the sketch, Talarico joked with actor James Austin Johnson's Trump character before delivering the show's traditional opening line.
body: During the show’s highly anticipated post-election episode, the upset-winning Lone Star State Democrat interrupted the President Trump character — played by James Austin Johnson — who was using the insult, “Talafreako,” discussing Tuesday’s midterm blue wave.
“That’s Senator ‘Talafreako,’” the real lawmaker-to-be said as he crashed the sketch and forced himself in front of Trump’s character.
“I’m James Talarico, the guy who’s been texting you every day asking for $5,” the newly elected Senator quipped.
“In this economy, who can blame you,” Johnson’s Trump said, poking his head behind the Democratic pol.

Talarico went on to explain how if the president and he “can work together, we can make life better for everyday Americans” because “it’s clear people want something new, they want something different.”

“I’m talking, of course, about ‘SNL’s cold opens. How many of these Trump freezers are they going to do,” Talarico questioned, seemingly taking a swipe at Johnson’s 50-odd appearances as the president during the show’s opening sketch.
“Infinity,” Johnson joked as Trump, before the pair yelled in unison, “Live from New York, it’s Saturday Night Live.”
Talarico won the Lone Star State’s race over Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton by securing just over 55% of the vote.

articles.headline: Another No 1 falls as Notre Dame hold off Miami to shake up college football playoff race
keyFacts: CJ Carr threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns as fourth-ranked Notre Dame defeated top-ranked Miami 31-24.
Miami coach Mario Cristobal stated he was beyond upset after officials ruled that a late fourth-down reception by Elija Lofton was incomplete.
Notre Dame will host Boston College next Saturday, while Miami will return home to face Duke.
body: CJ Carr threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns as No 4 Notre Dame avenged their most damaging loss of last season, racing to a 21-point lead before holding on to beat top-ranked Miami 31-24 on Saturday night.

Micah Gilbert caught two of Carr’s touchdown passes, Jordan Faison had the other and Nolan James Jr added a rushing score for Notre Dame (8-1, No 11 College Football Playoff), who entered the game knowing another defeat to Miami could derail their national championship hopes.

The Hurricanes (8-1, No 1 CFP) started slowly on offense in their first game without injured wide receiver and Heisman Trophy hopeful Malachi Toney. Notre Dame, whose 27-24 loss to Miami last season ultimately kept them out of the playoff, never trailed.

“I’m happy for this university,” Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman said in a televised on-field interview. “I’m happy for our players. There’s a lot of support from Notre Dame Nation and this is special moment for them. ... They’re a dang good football team and they beat a dang good football team.”

Darian Mensah threw three touchdown passes for Miami, twice bringing the Hurricanes within seven points after they had trailed 24-3 early in the third quarter. Cooper Barkate caught two of those passes, while Elija Lofton had the other.

Lofton nearly hauled in another touchdown that would have made it 31-30 – the same score as the teams’ famous 1988 meeting – with 3:36 remaining. He appeared to make a fourth-down catch in the end zone and get both feet down, but Notre Dame’s Luke Talich, who had intercepted Mensah in the third quarter, knocked the ball away.
Officials ruled that Lofton had not completed the catch. Notre Dame took over on downs, ran the clock down to about a minute and held on for the victory.
Miami coach Mario Cristobal said he was “beyond upset” that Lofton’s apparent catch had not been ruled a touchdown.
“Obviously, a tough loss to take,” Cristobal said. “Proud of our players for the resilience. ... Don’t leave it in the hands of the officials. Play better. Coach better. Find a way to win.”

Miami’s defeat left just two unbeaten teams in the Football Bowl Subdivision: Utah and UCLA, who both improved to 9-0 with victories on Saturday. It marked the first time since 2003 that only two teams had made it through their first nine games unbeaten, when TCU and Oklahoma achieved the feat.

A capacity crowd packed Notre Dame Stadium on a bitterly cold night, with temperatures falling from 40F at kickoff into the mid-30s. Forty-three NFL scouts were also in attendance as the Irish delivered their biggest victory of the season.

Miami had a chance to cut into Notre Dame’s lead in the second quarter after reaching first-and-goal at the Irish one-yard line. But three rushing attempts – one by Mark Fletcher Jr and two quarterback keepers by Mensah – went nowhere, forcing the Hurricanes to settle for a field goal.
Miami trailed 17-3 at halftime, having scored at least 14 first-half points and averaged 27 before the break in their first eight games.

Notre Dame also pulled out all the stops for the occasion, honoring a host of former stars including Joe Montana, Jerome Bettis Sr, Tony Rice, Chris Zorich, Ricky Watters and Ron Powlus. NBA president of basketball operations Byron Spruell was among those recognized, along with Pat Murphy, manager of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers and a former Notre Dame baseball coach.

The victory carried historical echoes of Notre Dame’s famous 31-30 upset of top-ranked Miami in the 1988 “Catholics vs Convicts” game. The Hurricanes fell to 44-7 all-time when ranked No 1 in the AP Top 25, including an 0-2 record against the Irish.

Notre Dame improved to 10-17-1 against No 1 teams, claiming their first such victory in exactly six years. Their previous win came against top-ranked Clemson on 7 November 2020, when the Tigers were without star quarterback Trevor Lawrence.
The Irish host Boston College next Saturday, while Miami return home to face Duke.

articles.headline: 10 Perfectly Designed Final Fantasy Magic Cards That Are 10/10, No Notes
keyFacts: Polygon reports that Wizards of the Coast adapted various characters, creatures, and moments from the Final Fantasy franchise into a Magic: The Gathering crossover set.
The article highlights ten specific card designs, such as Sin and Zack Fair, that incorporate lore elements and mechanics from across the Final Fantasy series.
Wizards of the Coast designed these cards to reflect source material traits like generational dread, tragic backstories, and signature franchise abilities.
body: Magic: The Gathering's Final Fantasy crossover set is a love letter to one of gaming's most enduring franchises, bringing together characters, creatures, locations, and iconic moments from across the series' history. With 16 mainline games and even more when counting sequels and spinoffs, Wizards of the Coast had quite the challenge in translating decades of RPG storytelling into a card game with its own language and mechanics.

Packed with hilarious nods, like Suplex, and incredible powerhouses, like Diamond Weapon, it comes as no surprise that Final Fantasy is among the best Universe Beyond sets in the game. But the most perfect designs among them capture a fundamental element of their source material, whether that's Bahamut's devastating Mega Flare, Phoenix Down's clutch resurrection, or the sheer spectacle of summoning Primal Odin.
Whether through clever mechanics or an inspired bit of flavor, these 10 Final Fantasy cards represent the very best of what this crossover has to offer.
10 Sin, Spira's Punishment

Sin anchors the legacy of Final Fantasy antagonists through crushing generational dread, and its card design captures that weight without relying on a lazy stat line. Whenever Sin, Spira's Punishment enters the battlefield or attacks, it exiles a random permanent card from your graveyard, creating a tapped token copy if it's a permanent and repeating the process if a land is hit. Sin is particularly nasty in Commander decks built around graveyard recursion and land synergies, especially when paired with cards like Adrix and Nev, Twincasters, which doubles the tokens it creates, or Hedron Crab, which helps stock the graveyard with fresh targets.

It's an unpredictable engine that turns the remnants of your battlefield into compounding threats throughout the game. Spira’s Punishment also evokes the inescapable cycle of destruction and rebirth that defines Final Fantasy 10, where Spira's people have endured a thousand years of Sin's devastation, rebuilding their lives after each attack and relying on Summoners to temporarily defeat the monster through a ritual sacrifice. Even its seven-mana cost feels entirely appropriate for a monster of its magnitude, though maybe 10 would’ve been more apropos.
9 Buster Sword

Weapons in gaming rarely carry the instant recognition of Cloud Strife's enormous Buster Sword — whether you picture it crudely strapped to his back during the bleak industrial sprawl of early Final Fantasy 7 or dragging it through the mud in Remake — but its significance extends well beyond its imposing silhouette. Passed down through Angeal, Zack, and eventually Cloud, the sword represents the heavy burden of legacy and what one generation leaves behind for another.

Magic: The Gathering captures some of that history through its equipment design, with the Buster Sword giving its wielder a substantial power boost of +3/+2. Whenever said creature hits an opponent directly, you draw a card, then get the opportunity to cast a spell from your hand for free, provided its mana value doesn't exceed the damage dealt. It's a suitably devastating reward for landing a direct hit, and a fitting tribute to one of Final Fantasy's most enduring symbols.
8 Jumbo Cactuar

At first glance, Cactuars look like little more than walking houseplants, but when crossed, they can hit you with a devastating flurry of needles. Among Final Fantasy's most recognizable recurring monsters, Cactuars have made a career out of looking harmless before delivering some devastating blows, similar to the goofy-looking Tonberries. MTG’s Jumbo Cactuar follows that lineage beautifully through a seven-mana creature with a relatively unassuming 1/7 stat line. It looks like any regular green common creature, until you notice its ability, 10,000 Needles, which gives it a whopping +9,999/+0 whenever it attacks.

That's right, this seemingly harmless plant suddenly becomes a 10,000-power monster capable of flattening just about anything in its path. It's an almost comically literal interpretation of the Cactuar family's signature attack, and that's what makes it so brilliant (and hilarious). There's no need for elaborate transformations or complicated synergies. Magic simply takes one of Final Fantasy's most recognizable monster abilities and turns it into a devastating combat trick.
7 Lightning, Army of One

While Final Fantasy 13 remains one of the most divisive entries in the franchise’s storied history, Lightning herself stands tall as one of its absolute finest protagonists. She’s a relentless soldier defined by unwavering resolve and immediate action, a former Guardian Corps sergeant who goes AWOL during the violent exile of Bodhum's citizens, derailing a Purge train and battling through the Hanging Edge to rescue her sister.

Her Magic card captures that uncompromising spirit right out of the gate. A three-mana creature with first strike, trample, and lifelink is already a formidable combatant, but her stagger ability is what makes the design sing. Whenever Lightning, Army of One deals combat damage to an opponent, all damage dealt to that player and their permanents by any source is doubled until your next turn. It’s a brilliant adaptation of FF13’s defining combat rhythm, where staggering an enemy leaves them completely exposed to devastating follow-up attacks. Magic turns her into the tip of the spear for an all-out assault, translating one of the series' signature mechanics into a game-winning tactical engine.
6 Zack Fair

Zack Fair's story is one of Final Fantasy 7’s most heartbreaking, particularly because his final moments have such a profound impact on Cloud's journey. Magic honors the character with a 0/1 legendary creature that enters with a +1/+1 counter on it. You can play one mana to sacrifice Zack Fair and give another creature indestructible, Zack’s counters, and even the equipment attached to him.

It's a thoughtful piece of design that essentially turns his death into an act of protection and inheritance. There's no elaborate transformation or complicated combination of abilities, Zack's final act becomes a playable mechanic, allowing another hero to carry his strength and equipment forward. It’s hard to imagine a more poignant tribute to a character whose entire legacy is defined by passing the torch, and some players have found clever ways to abuse it by looping him from the graveyard with reanimation engines like Sun Titan or Lurrus, repeatedly granting their board indestructible while constantly passing his stat boosts down the line.
5 Aerith Gainsborough

Aerith’s power has always stemmed from gentle resilience rather than overwhelming force. She’s a healer, after all, and the last surviving Cetra, hiding in plain sight selling flowers in the Sector 5 slums while carrying the solitary burden of the Planet's survival. In Magic, Aerith Gainsborough is a 2/2 legendary creature that enters the battlefield with lifelink, and whenever you gain life, she receives a +1/+1 counter. This makes her progressively stronger as she supports your other creatures and keeps your life total at a healthy advantage over your opponents.

However, the real stroke of genius comes when Aerith dies. Every legendary creature you control receives +1/+1 counters equal to the number Aerith had accumulated during her time on the battlefield. It's a beautiful mechanical interpretation of her legacy, particularly considering the profound impact her death has on Cloud and the rest of the party in the original game. Aerith's influence doesn't disappear when she's gone, but lives on through the people she leaves behind. And it’s even better when you’ve already got a 12/12 Eldrazi on the board.
4 Yuna, Hope of Spira

Final Fantasy 10’s Yuna is a summoner first and foremost, making her one of the most natural candidates for a Magic card built around enchantments and their associated creatures. What makes Yuna, Hope of Spira particularly clever is how the card encourages players to assemble a collection of saga creatures, the special enchantments introduced in the Final Fantasy set to represent the franchise's iconic summons.

During your turn, Yuna grants herself and your other enchantment creatures trample, lifelink, and ward 2, making the entire group considerably more difficult to deal with. She can also return an enchantment from your graveyard to the battlefield at the end of your turn, but with a finality counter on it that prevents it from returning to the graveyard again. It's a fantastic representation of Yuna's role as a summoner, turning her into the centerpiece of an entire Aeon-focused strategy with enchantment creatures cards like Yojimbo, Bahamut, Knights of Round, and more.
3 Summon: Knights of Round

Speaking of Knights of Round, it's as much a powerful Magic card as it is a legendary summon in the games. First appearing as the ultimate secret Materia in Final Fantasy 7, tucked away on the unmapped Round Island and requiring a Gold Chocobo just to reach, it calls forth 13 holy knights to rain down an unskippable two-minute-long assault of apocalyptic damage. It was the absolute pinnacle of endgame excess, forcing players to sit back and watch a cinematic spectacle unfold while Sephiroth’s health bar disintegrated.

Magic’s interpretation of it is every bit as theatrical. Designed as an eight-mana Saga creature, Knights of Round gradually builds an army by creating three 2/2 Knight tokens across each of its first four chapters. That’s twelve knights in total, before its fifth and final chapter delivers Ultimate End, buffing your entire board with +2/+2 and dropping an indestructible counter onto each of your creatures. It's a wonderfully patient piece of design that rewards players for waiting out the full summon sequence, turning that notoriously long animation into a looming, game-ending countdown your opponents can only watch in dread. Unless they’re in blue, of course.
2 Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER/Sephiroth, One-Winged Angel

Sephiroth’s transformation from celebrated First Class SOLDIER hero to the cold One-Winged Angel remains one of gaming’s most devastating character arcs. He wasn't just a villain; he was Shinra's ultimate hero whose sanity shattered the moment he uncovered his horrific origins inside the Nibelheim mansion: he was engineered from the alien calamity Jenova. He burned Nibelheim to the ground and began viewing humanity as mere parasites. His tragic fall shifted the entire scope of Final Fantasy 7 from an anti-corporate resistance story into an apocalyptic cosmic horror.

Magic imbues that journey onto a double-faced creature that grows more dangerous as the battlefield descends into chaos. On his front side, Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER allows you to sacrifice another creature whenever he enters or attacks, drawing a card in return. Meanwhile, whenever another creature dies, you drain one life from an opponent and gain one yourself. Once that second ability has resolved for the fourth time in a single turn, Sephiroth transforms into his One-Winged Angel form, granting an emblem that keeps the life-drain engine running permanently whenever creatures die. You can also even stack that with his second ability, letting you sac as many creatures as you like in exchange for that many card draws. It's an inspired way to represent Sephiroth's growing power, turning the battlefield into a ticking clock as his enemies fall around him.
1 Absolute Virtue

Final Fantasy 11 has no shortage of formidable enemies, but few developed the same legendary reputation as Absolute Virtue. This optional superboss became infamous for its extraordinary durability and punishing difficulty, earning a reputation as one of the most frustrating encounters in the entire franchise. Absolute Virtue could repeatedly unleash powerful abilities borrowed from multiple player classes, including Benediction, which allowed it to restore enormous amounts of health just when victory seemed within reach. Its substantial passive regeneration made matters even worse, turning the encounter into an exhausting war of attrition that demanded meticulous coordination from an entire alliance of players. Some groups spent more than 18 hours attempting to defeat it, cementing its place in MMO history as one of gaming's most notorious boss encounters.

Magic distills its intimidating presence through an eight-mana 8/8 construction that can't be countered when it’s played, plus it has flying, of course. Even more terrifying is its secondary ability, which grants you protection from each of your opponents, effectively making you untouchable while Absolute Virtue remains on the battlefield. Opponents can’t attack you, target you with spells, or even enchant you. It's a fitting translation of a boss that once seemed practically impossible to defeat, forcing opponents to find a way around its defenses before they can even think about bringing it down.

articles.headline: Tomorrow's Top 25 Today: Georgia reclaims No. 1 spot, Tennessee joins top 10 in college football rankings
keyFacts: Georgia is projected to return to the No. 1 spot in the updated AP Top 25 poll following a win at Ole Miss.
Notre Dame secured a 31-24 victory against Miami, which impacts both teams' positions in the upcoming college football rankings.
The updated AP Top 25 poll will be officially released on Sunday following a chaotic Week 10 of college football games.
body: When you have seven different games between teams that were just announced in the top 25 of the new College Football Playoff Rankings, the postseason outlook hung in the balance throughout a chaotic Week 10. The day provided some massive wins for top teams, certainly, but also yet another change at No. 1.

Notre Dame's 31-24 win against Miami will open up the top spot for debate regarding the best team in college football. We will have to wait until Tuesday night to hear from the College Football Playoff Selection Committee, but fans get their first look at the new landscape with the release of an updated AP Top 25 poll on Sunday.

We project that Georgia will move up into the No. 1 spot in the wake of an impressive wire-to-wire win at Ole Miss on Saturday night, edging out a Utah team that will certainly have a case with its 9-0 record and its own high-quality Week 10 win against BYU. The AP voters had a closer gap between Georgia and Miami than they did between Georgia and Utah, and those signals point to the Bulldogs keeping that margin to the tune of returning to the No. 1 spot just ahead of the Utes.

As for the Fighting Irish, beating Miami provides an interesting moment in rankings analysis because of the disparity between the AP poll and the College Football Playoff Rankings. Notre Dame was slotted at No. 11 by the selection committee and in that lens, should be poised for a big move up after beating No. 1.

The only problem? Notre Dame was already up in a top position in the eyes of the AP voters at No. 4, and that leaves much less room for a big move up in those rankings despite the impressive and much-needed win.

Other winners from the ranked-on-ranked games will see some notable improvements in the AP poll, including moves up for Tennessee and Alabama after double-digit wins against other ranked SEC foes. It's going to also put a spotlight on the cut line for a top 25 ballot, as teams like Ole Miss and LSU fight for inclusion after taking their third loss of the season.
Here's how we think the new AP Top 25 poll will look on Sunday after Week 10:

1. Georgia (Last week -- 2): After thrashing Ole Miss, the Bulldogs are set to return to the No. 1 spot. Georgia reached No. 1 earlier this season for a one-week residence before the upset loss to Auburn, and now that stunning, turnover-filled defeat is the lone blemish on a resume that is otherwise highlighted by wins over Alabama, Ole Miss and Florida.

2. Utah (3): There was already one brave AP poll voter who had Utah as their No. 1 team coming into the week, and we're projecting that they'll have more company after the Utes emerged victorious in a 28-20 thriller against rival BYU.

3. Notre Dame (4): As we mentioned earlier, it's extremely difficult to know exactly how the AP voters will react to the differences in their rankings and the selection committee's decisions. In Notre Dame's case, there is an instinct to improve their position from No. 11, but voters individually don't have much room to move the Fighting Irish up on their ballots if the team was at No. 4 last week.

4. UCLA (5): The great power of the Bruins' ranking remains as Bob Chesney's crew improved to 9-0 with a win at Minnesota. The victory added to an impressive series of road performances for UCLA, and also included a wild second half showing from quarterback Ty Dieffenbach. The Bruins' starter finished with 303 passing yards and three touchdowns on just eight completions behind explosive pass plays of 75, 75, 54 and 27 yards, with three of those coming after halftime.

5. Miami (1): A close loss on the road to another top team has its limits for rankings punishment. That is especially true when it's early November, the first loss of the season, and it also comes without your star wide receiver because of a recent injury. Miami could fall lower, but it's hard to imagine an 8-1 team with obvious quality loss dropping behind multiple two-loss teams.

6. Alabama (9): The AP voters already had Alabama as the top two-loss team in the country last week, but that status is now undeniable after the Crimson Tide pulled away from LSU for a 31-13 win in Baton Rouge. Kalen DeBoer's team got off to a strong start and stayed in control most of the afternoon, then finished on a 21-0 run the moment LSU got its first lead of the game. The win adds to victories against Kentucky and South Carolina, building a solid resume even against other teams with fewer losses.
7. Indiana (6): The Hoosiers were off in Week 10 and will be back in action next week at home against USC.

8. Texas (10): There is not a ton of room for upward movement after a hard-fought road win at Missouri, but the Longhorns definitely strengthened their resume with the road win. Though the Tigers could fall from the top 25 after the defeat, it's still a quality win that will bolster Texas' status as a top-10 team.

9. Tennessee (16): This is admittedly a big jump up in the rankings but one that could be warranted after both a 34-6 point win against Kentucky and also the success of Alabama at LSU. The Vols could ultimately be held back from jumping ahead of Alabama because of the head-to-head loss to Texas, but anything between No. 6 and No. 10 is fair game for a Tennessee team that is 7-2 with a pair of top-end wins against teams that were ranked in the top 10 at the time.
10. Texas Tech (13): The Red Raiders are currently in action against West Virginia.
11. Wake Forest (14): Starting quarterback Gio Lopez was able to spend an extra week getting healthy for the final push of the season as his Demon Deacon teammates crushed FCS Merrimack 77-0.

12. BYU (7): The Cougars could end up getting credit for their competitiveness in a 28-20 loss at Utah that had more than a couple of self-inflicted wounds preventing the upset rivalry win. BYU had a 20-0 run in the middle of this game but saw its last effort end on a Bear Bachmeier interception that dropped the Cougars to 7-2 overall. The win against Notre Dame clearly serves as the strongest resume point for BYU, but the playoff conversation in general is getting late early with two conference losses and few quality win opportunities left.

13. Kentucky (8): Wins against LSU and South Carolina keep the floor pretty high for Kentucky, but it should be noted the AP voters were a bit lower on the Wildcats than the selection committee. So the drop to No. 13 is really just a five-spot drop for the AP voters, while it would be a seven-spot drop from their CFP Rankings placement of No. 6.

14. Houston (17): The Cougars improved to 7-2 after surviving a good test from Cincinnati, holding on for a 31-24 win behind three total touchdowns from Conner Weigman. Houston is working with a bit of a quality loss resume, with unranked Oklahoma State as its best win, but their quality has held up across nine games, and the only two losses are each by one score to other ranked teams on the road (Utah, Texas Tech).

15. Oregon (NR): The Ducks were ranked in the College Football Playoff Selection Committee top 25 and will absolutely be set for a return to the AP poll after a 41-28 win in Columbus against Ohio State. It's unclear whether the reaction will be stronger for Oregon after the win or the Buckeyes after the loss, but a 6-3 record with wins over Ohio State, USC and Boise State is a solid resume for top 25 consideration.
16. USC (18): The Trojans were off in Week 10 and will be back in action next week at Indiana.

17. Ohio State (11): The AP voters are not tasked with the same injury consideration protocols the in the same way as the College Football Playoff Selection Committee, and thus we're not projecting Saturday's loss to Oregon to be treated as anything other than a defeat to another Big Ten title contender. Wins against Indiana and Iowa serve as the best buffer to keep Ohio State from a rankings free-fall.

18. Boise State (20): The Broncos did not have starting quarterback Maddux Madsen due to injury, but that did not stop the team from putting 64 points on the board against a Colorado State team that has gotten picked apart in Pac-12 play. Now 8-1 overall, Boise State's attention turns to its home stretch of the season, which includes the first-ever Pac-12 flex week at the end of November with a matchup yet to be determined for Week 13.

19. Iowa (21): A road test at Northwestern proved to be yet another resume point for an Iowa team that continues to handle its business. The Hawkeyes have wins over Northwestern, Wisconsin and Michigan, and just two losses on the season to Ohio State and Minnesota. It's not a resume that overwhelms voters, but in a season that lacks consistency there is something comforting about Iowa's 7-2 profile.

20. New Mexico (22): The Lobos are going to keep the historic AP ranking the program achieved last week, but the margins around the cut line are slim enough to be concerned about giving up a spot in the consensus rankings. Teams like Oregon and Ohio State occupying spaces in the 20s make it tough for New Mexico to win some of those tiebreaker resume debates, even if their 8-1 record is two games better than those preseason title picks.

21. South Carolina (23): The winning streak continues with South Carolina now up to four wins in a row since starting 0-3 in SEC play. The Gamecocks' victory against Texas A&M in Columbia isn't going to move the voters individually, but the collective appreciation of South Carolina's late-season form will continue to get respect, and the win against Tennessee certainly holds more weight now for the argument that this should be among the highest-ranked three-loss teams in the country.

22. Ole Miss (12): Not only did the Rebels lose in a great opportunity with Georgia in town, but Ole Miss' resume took a hit with the results from SEC play in Week 10. Wins against both LSU and Missouri take on less weight after both of those teams are headed down, if not out, in the rankings, as Ole Miss seems destined to get pinned with similar three-loss teams near the edge of the top 25.

23. Arizona (24): Unranked by the College Football Playoff Selection Committee but ranked by the AP voters last week, the Wildcats are going to be right on the cut line after needing a late onside kick and field goal to avoid an upset against TCU. Arizona does stand out with its 7-2 record, but its best win came against Cincinnati, and it's 0-2 against other ranked teams this season.

24. LSU (15): There is an argument to drop LSU from the top 25 based on an absence of high-quality wins, but we aren't projecting that reaction from the AP voters. Lane Kiffin's Tigers will have an opportunity to win their way back up the rankings with matchups against Texas and Tennessee in the coming weeks, but for now, LSU has just three SEC wins against opponents who have a combined 6-14 record in conference play. Voters might not drop LSU from No. 15 all the way out for losing a national title contender, but the Tigers are absolutely on notice if they can't win out.

25. SMU (NR): The Mustangs improved to 7-2 with an eye-popping 51-28 win against Virginia Tech on Friday night in Dallas. The victory sets up the potential for an appearance in the top 25 ahead of a massive showdown with Wake Forest in Week 11.
Projected to drop out: No. 19 Missouri, No. 25 Florida

articles.headline: Path of Exile 2 Duelist class preview: I’ve got blood to bleed
keyFacts: Destructoid previewed the new Duelist class and fifth Act of Path of Exile 2 at ExileCon 2026.
The Duelist class features blood-infused dual-wielding, new stances, parrying mechanics, and a customizable squire companion.
Path of Exile 2 is scheduled for release on Dec. 11 alongside the 1.0 patch.
body: Today at ExileCon 2026, I had the amazing chance to demo Path of Exile 2 ‘s new Duelist class, set to come out alongside the game’s 1.0 patch. I got a sneak peek into the game’s fifth Act, too, which I can say is more grim and dark than most things you’ve seen in PoE 2 so far (and that’s saying a lot ).

The version of the Duelist I played is of the Knight ascendancy, though I did not dabble in the implications and details of this ascendancy just yet (we did only have 30 minutes and that was with a pre-equipped level 54 character). What I did do, however, is carve through hundreds of mobs using two dual-wielded short swords which were empowered by a blood infusion allowing me to parry enemy attacks to gather blood and then unleash it upon them with ultra violence.

With the stances, I could use right-click to cut through the mob group and then take up a stance, which is a new mechanic tied to the duelist. Basically, if you hold right click and do the full attack, some of your next abilities can be empowered, which in this case I used to empower my blood slash and inflict copious amount of bleed stacks on the enemy. These particular stacks do not proc on their own or over time, but they can build up quite a lot, allowing you to use a quick blink-slash on an enemy with pent up crimson and chunk them for a lot of their HP.
Image via GGG Subscribe to our newsletter for special daily updates live from the floor of ExileCon 2026!

Of course, you can still inflict regular bleed on enemies, but softening them up for one crushing blow is basically the name of the game here. Utilizing parries you can gather blood to your sword, which you can then release on enemies to build up a lot of bleed and do great AOE blood damage if you are fighting groups. Do not let the word “parry” confuse you here, though: it’s not Sekiro where you need to perfectly time your blocks, that would be silly for a game of this kind. No, parrying simply requires you to hold block when enemies are attacking you, and that’s that, but its audio-visual cues still make each parry satisfying.

But this is not the only side of the Duelist that I got to see. The Knight ascendancy is all about honor and glory, meaning you can get your own standard and banner and place them down to give yourself a lot of cool effects, as well as to inflict enemies with all sorts of debuffs and damage effects. And a knight is simply incomplete without a squire, whom you can have following you around and fighting by your side. You are responsible for him, of course, and as such must give him weapons, armor, and skills, which you should choose carefully to make sure he synergizes with your own build.

The blood build up is a great combination shown by Jonathan Rogers himself yesterday during the keynote, since you could use your own blood-infused weapons to build up stacks on enemies and let your trusty sidekick chunk them for you.

I loved how the squire worked overall, but I must say I preferred the speed and the pure carnage caused by the solo dual-wielder. At any rate, both are amazing options and are just scratching the surface of what this class is going to be, since it is very obvious that GGG put in tremendous amounts of effort into making 1.0 as big and as good as it can possibly be.
Path of Exile 2 comes out on Dec. 11 and will introduce two new classes: the Duelist and the Shadow , alongside hundreds if not thousands of other changes and additions.

articles.headline: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike
keyFacts: Houthi-linked media reported that Saudi air strikes killed at least 33 people and injured 39 in Yemen on Saturday.
Fighting between Houthis and Saudi-backed forces recently resumed, killing over 1,600 people according to the United Nations.
Houthi leader Mahdi al-Mashat vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.
body: - Published
Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say at least 33 people, including women and children, have been killed in air strikes by Saudi Arabia.
There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.

Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.
The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins.
The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital.
Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Saturday. It added that 39 people had been injured.
The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.
The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war.
A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plane landing there.

The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.
Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen.
On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people.
The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.
The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities.
Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh.
A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

articles.headline: Dana White responds to question about Trump’s White House press secretary request
keyFacts: President Donald Trump offered UFC CEO Dana White the position of White House press secretary in a Truth Social post.
White said he is flying to Washington to meet with Trump on Monday, noting that he already has many jobs.
White also posted an image of himself at a White House podium on Instagram captioned 'Onto the next chapter.'
body: Dana White , the CEO of the UFC and a longtime ally of President Donald Trump , responded to a question on Saturday night about the president saying he should serve as his next White House press secretary .

While taking questions from reporters at a boxing event in London, White said he is flying to Washington, D.C., “right now” when he was asked for his reaction to the post and further details. White also said he will meet with the president on Monday and that he “has a lot of jobs already.”

It is unclear whether Trump was joking about the Saturday afternoon offer, as the key position has remained unfilled since Katie Zacharia’s five-day stint in the role, and White would be an untraditional and unprecedented choice. Trump hosted a UFC event on the White House lawn over the summer as part of the America 250 celebrations.

“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job as Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump wrote in the Truth Social post. “Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!”

Though White didn’t overtly answer the reporter’s question, he posted what appeared to be an AI-generated image of him standing behind the White House podium on his Instagram story with the caption “Onto the next chapter” following Trump’s post.
TRUMP OFFERS WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY POSITION TO DANA WHITE

The president has long touted his relationships with celebrities in both his first and second terms. He campaigned with rap mogul Nicki Minaj and retired boxing legend Mike Tyson ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, and has spoken often about how he used to be friendly with Democratic figures before deciding to run for president in 2016.

Trump hasn’t publicly commented much on his plans to replace Zacharia in recent weeks. Karoline Leavitt, who held the position before resigning in August to spend more time with her family, was widely viewed as an extremely successful member of the Trump administration.

articles.headline: Path of Exile 2's game director thinks a death recap will finally allow us players to complain about the right things
keyFacts: Game director Jonathan Rogers confirmed that a death recap screen is coming to Path of Exile 2.
The feature will be included in the full 1.0 release scheduled for December 11.
Rogers stated the recap will help players identify character weaknesses and give specific feedback on monster balance.
body: I've been playing Path of Exile for almost ten years and have put a ton of hours into PoE2 since it entered early access, and in all that time there's one feature that I've wished for more than any other. More than stash tabs, more than fancy microtransactions, even more than finally finding a mirror in the wild.

What I want more than anything is a death recap: a way to finally have some idea why my turbo powerful character that's blasting through a map went pop. At an interview at ExileCon this weekend, game director Jonathan Rogers confirmed that it's finally coming to Path of Exile 2.

I don't know whether Grinding Gear intended to announce the feature this weekend, but during the keynote's live demo of new content, Mark Roberts' character died. And there before our eyes, live and in person, was a death recap screen. After we all got done cheering, Rogers laughed and confirmed that the feature was present and would be included in the full 1.0 release coming up on December 11.

"I was really worried that it wasn't going to be useful enough or accurate enough, but we got it to a place that I'm fairly happy with," Rogers said when I asked him to confirm that the feature would be present at launch.
"The thing that's not quite good is the damage over time tracking," he added. "We do tell you that you took it but we don't know where it came from.”
Thankfully, it's a bit easier to parse taking damage over time in the game already, and he assured us that they're working on getting that sorted out as well.

One of the reasons that the death recap is such an important feature is that it can be incredibly hard to parse exactly what you should be focusing on with your character once you get to the endgame. A lot of times you've maxed your resistances, have a decent life pool, and a good amount of either armour, evasion, or energy shield, but still something comes along and explodes you. And since there are often many monsters on the screen, to say nothing of all the explosions or arrows or minions or ice comets that you yourself are spamming, it can be almost impossible to figure out what happened.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"The most important thing to be was like… here's the damage you took and how much of it was mitigated," says Rogers. "My goal was to drive you toward 'what is the thing I need to fix about my character to have avoided this.'" A big physical hit? Maybe some more evasion or life. Cold damage? Maybe grab a couple jewels with + to max cold res.
Sometimes though, the problem isn't with you. Sometimes you get a killer crab that kills hundreds of thousands of players due to a typo. He thinks the death recap will help here, too.

"This may sound a bit funny, but I think it'll actually give our players an avenue to complain about the correct things. Sometimes we just have monsters that have wrong balance values, it happens, and in the heat of battle you don't know what it was. Now you'll be able to say this particular monster is the one that has the damage that's off the hook and then it allows them to direct us to that."
Despite having their own internal systems to monitor monster behavior, nothing beats the urgency and immediacy of a legion of players crying out at once on the internet about killer crabs.
Mark Roberts went on to say that he anticipates that the feature "will 100% be asked for en masse" by Path of Exile 1 players, and if it is, they'll port that functionality over as soon as they can.
As for me, the death recap is but one of many amazing features I'm looking forward to in Path of Exile 2's full release. It will be available on December 11th.

articles.headline: Syncing Apple Music across your devices is easier than you think
keyFacts: Apple Music is available on multiple platforms like Android and Windows, but users must ensure they are signed into the same Apple Account on all devices.
Users can sync their music library across devices by enabling the Sync Library setting in the Apple Music app or device settings.
If syncing fails, users can update their cloud library, check their Wi-Fi connection, or toggle the Sync Library setting off and back on.
body: Syncing Apple Music across your devices is easier than you think
Using Apple Music on multiple devices? Keeping them in sync is a breeze.

Apple Music is one of the best music streaming platforms right now, especially for Apple device owners. But despite its association with the tech giant, Apple Music is not exclusive to Apple devices and is available on multiple platforms. You can, for example, sign in with your Apple Account and listen to your favorite songs on an Android phone, Windows PC or even smart TVs.

After signing in on a new device, though, you may notice that your music library isn't synced and your songs aren't there. If this has happened to you, don't worry. Changing a single setting in Apple Music will prompt it to sync your music across all your devices, ensuring you don't have to manage your library manually on each one.
How to turn on Sync Library on Apple Music

The main reason Apple Music might not sync your library across devices is that you're using different accounts on each device, so check that first. If you're not sure which account you're using, open the Apple Music app and tap your profile picture on the Home tab. If the email address on the unsynced device doesn't match, you're signed in on a different account. Sign out, then log in using your primary Apple Account.

Now make sure Sync Library is enabled on your devices. On your iPhone or iPad, open Settings and look for Apps. Then, find the Music app in the list and enable Sync Library. On a Mac, open the Music app and click the "Music" menu at the top of the screen, then go to Settings. Now, under the General tab, make sure Sync Library is enabled and click OK to save your settings. The process is pretty much the same in Windows, but you need to click the three-dot button instead to find Settings. If you have an Android phone, this option is enabled by default, and you don't need to change anything.

No matter the platform, the first sync might take a while, especially if you have a large music library. If you don't see your songs right away after enabling syncing, leave the Music app open and wait a few minutes.
What to do when Apple Music won't sync

In the Mac app, click the File menu, then go to Library and select Update Cloud Library — this will force the app to sync and check for updates in your personal library. This option is also available in the Windows app and can be found in the sidebar. Unfortunately, the Android and iOS apps don't have that option.

Also, make sure your mobile devices are connected to Wi-Fi and not in Low Power Mode, as this may prevent them from syncing your music library. If nothing else has worked, your best option is to go back to Settings, turn off Sync Library and then turn it back on. You can also try signing out of your Apple Account and logging back in. If you don't subscribe to Apple Music and have an offline library on your Mac or PC, the only way to sync your library is to manually transfer the Music folder to another computer via Apple iTunes or Apple Devices.

Syncing behavior isn't the only setting you might want to change in Apple Music. While you're there, it's worth exploring some other toggles, like changing the audio quality options to enable lossless audio.

articles.headline: Just a moonshot? Google energy head claims data centers in space would cost up to 100x more than on Earth
keyFacts: Google global head of data center energy Amanda Peterson Corio stated that space data centers could cost up to 100 times more than terrestrial facilities.
Corio advised exploring terrestrial options first, noting that the primary bottleneck on Earth is permitting rather than a lack of power.
The remarks contrast with SpaceX's plans to deploy numerous data-center satellites, though both companies' financial and technical timelines remain unproven.
body: - Google global head of data center energy says space data centers could cost up to 100 times more than terrestrial ones
- Amanda Peterson Corio's remarks came weeks after Google launched its first Suncatcher prototype, a roughly 1kW satellite that has since run Gemma 4 on an orbiting TPU, one chip at a time
- Corio says the real bottleneck on Earth is permitting rather than power, the same politics that backers of orbital compute claim they can escape
Google has spent the past month showing off AI chips working in orbit, but the executive responsible for powering its data centers back on Earth has just put a sobering price on the idea.

Speaking at The Information's recent WTF Summit in Napa Valley, Amanda Peterson Corio, Google's global head of data center energy, said data centers in space could cost up to 100 times as much as those built on the ground.
Her advice to the rest of the industry was simple and (pun intended) grounded: "Let's explore all the terrestrial options before we go extraterrestrial."
A very expensive proposition?

The remarks land at an awkward moment, because Google is testing exactly this kind of hardware right now. Its first Project Suncatcher prototype, built with satellite operator Planet, launched on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission on October 1.

Google recently also announced its Hello World milestone: an onboard Gemma 4 model, running on a TPU, wrote a short haiku about being in space, which was downlinked as the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway.

The company bills this as the first AI response from a data center-class TPU in orbit. That is a carefully measured claim, given that Starcloud put an Nvidia H100 into orbit a year ago and was running AI models on it within weeks.

Scale is the bigger caveat and one that can be easily overlooked amidst the hype: The satellite carries four TPUs but generates only about 1kW of solar power, so it can run just one chip at a time for roughly 20 minutes per session, according to The Next Web. A single 1 GW AI campus, the kind now under construction on the ground, draws about a million times that much power.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!

Google has described Suncatcher as a "moonshot" since it was unveiled a year ago, and project lead Travis Beals told NPR on launch day that he did not expect orbital compute to become cheaper than the terrestrial kind within the next five years.
Not the first or last skeptic of orbital datacenters

This did start a somewhat interesting conversation on Wall Street; Short seller Jim Chanos read Corio's statement as $5 trillion per gigawatt of compute, and posted on X that the gap between her view and the estimates of SpaceX management and bulls "should give pause to anyone trying to model this business out."

TIKR pushed the arithmetic further by examining recent claims: SpaceX's CFO told investors last month that new compute pays for itself in under a year at current rental rates. Built in orbit at up to 100 times the cost and rented at the same price, TIKR calculated that payback stretches to as long as a century, or about a decade even at a tenth of Corio's stated ceiling.

That matters because orbital compute underpins part of SpaceX's roughly $1.8 trillion market value at the time of writing. The company has asked the FCC for permission to launch up to a million data-center satellites, and Musk has posted that the orbital compute SpaceX deploys each month will probably overtake terrestrial compute around the end of 2028. Yet SpaceX's own IPO paperwork warned investors of "significant technical complexity and unproven technologies," and said its orbital data centers might never become commercially viable.

Corio is hardly the first skeptic. OpenAI's Sam Altman called the idea "ridiculous" under current conditions earlier this year, even as Nvidia lined up a Space-1 Vera Rubin module aimed squarely at orbital data centers.

This is an extremely interesting take from Google's end. Alphabet is one of SpaceX's largest outside shareholders, with a stake disclosed at 6.11% at the end of 2025, according to Bloomberg, and Google has reportedly been in talks with SpaceX about launching future Suncatcher hardware. Its energy chief has questioned and potentially poured cold water on a thesis that props up part of an asset Alphabet owns, while Google's own moonshot depends on cheap SpaceX launches arriving on schedule.

Corio's broader argument, somewhat ironically, was about the ground rather than the sky. According to The Information, she said the US has enough power and that the real bottlenecks are permitting and grid interconnection studies.

She blamed much of the local backlash against data centers on newer, less experienced developers, without naming any, and said Google prepays for grid upgrades over 15 to 20 years in more than 9 states, posts restoration bonds, and has stopped using nondisclosure agreements with local governments.

There is, however, a problem with this argument: Established firms such as Oracle have also faced local resistance, which complicates the idea that inexperienced newcomers are the problem. The backlash is anything but marginal: opposition has spread across the US, and Data Center Watch counted 75 projects worth about $130 billion delayed or blocked in the first quarter of 2026 alone.

There is a political angle built around these arguments that keeps orbital data centers in play, and SpaceX is essentially building on that promise. After this week's midterm elections, in which data center construction was a campaign issue in several races, including the contest for Texas governor, Musk posted, "Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now."

Leaving the planet does not, however, mean leaving the permit queue; SpaceX's million-satellite request and Blue Origin's 51,600-satellite Project Sunrise both need FCC approval, and debris and spectrum concerns give regulators and rivals plenty to object to, just at a higher altitude. If power really is plentiful and permission is the bottleneck, as Corio argues, then orbit's main selling point is jumping that queue, and by her numbers it is a very expensive way to do it.

For now, until someone flies more than a kilowatt-scale test bed and publishes what it actually costs, the multiple between orbit and the ground, whether it turns out to be 3x, 10x, or as much as 100x, remains an educated guess. Corio's stated ceiling is arguably as unproven as Musk's timetable. Only one of those numbers, however, is already priced in considerably into a stock's current valuation, and SpaceX investors will be waiting for financials to back its CEO's claims with bated breath to say the least.

articles.headline: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?
keyFacts: Nintendo released a remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time that plays very similarly to the original 1998 N64 classic.
Developers made adjustments to enhanced scary elements after test players reported that the updated graphics made certain areas too frightening.
Nintendo also made the Water Temple easier by allowing players to change heavy boots easily and leverage camera orientation.
body: - Published
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was finally released on Thursday, after years of rumours that Nintendo would remake the game - considered one of the best ever made.
IGN called it "the biggest game of the decade" in their review, external when it launched in 1998 on the N64, and it set the standard for 3D games.

A lot of the things we take for granted in modern games - such as riding a horse, fighting with a sword and shield, or locking on to enemies with the tap of a button - were pioneered or perfected in Ocarina of Time.
It received an almost perfect score from critics and, decades on, remains the highest-rated game in history on Metacritic, which aggregates reviews.
So how do you remake what many consider a masterpiece?
Those like me who grew up playing the original will feel right at home here.
Nintendo has decided against reinventing the wheel, instead producing something which plays very similarly to the N64 classic.

As I've said before, video game remakes are a bit different to film or TV - gaming fans often clamour for a new take on their favourites, hoping developers harness evolution in tech to make them fresh.
And games have come a long way in the almost 30 years since the original Ocarina of Time came out.

"When you compare the games in the past and the games in modern times, so to speak, the norms of what people expect from a game have evolved naturally," Nintendo producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi told me.
"In the past, games where the users may have needed more imagination to fill the blanks or the gaps are now clearly expressed through the graphics that they see on the screen."

But fancy graphics have come at a price - a pivot away from realism into something a bit more cartoonish. Some might even be disappointed by this, given the N64 game had quite horrifying elements in places.
One was the Skulltula House, a room where people had been morphed into human-spider hybrids.

"Back when we created the original Ocarina of Time, the means to convey or express ideas was limited compared with what we have now," series producer Eiji Aonuma - who worked on the original game - said.
"With regard to even the so-called scary elements, we strove to add a touch of the comical."
But he told the BBC that enhanced graphics and lighting capabilities unintentionally exaggerated the already-spooky Skulltula House and its potential to strike fear into players.

"When we carried out the test play, the testers were telling us, 'Oh, this is too scary'," he said. "So of course, in the end product, we've made the necessary adjustments so that we can retain the same balance that we had achieved in the original."
'Serious thought has gone into every decision'
I spoke to a few YouTubers about the upcoming game to get their thoughts - and the response was overwhelmingly positive.
Mike Channell, co-editor of the YouTube channel Outside Xbox, said he believed the remake had been made "very meticulously" in the hopes of living up to fan expectations.

"Having played the game, it's clear that serious thought has gone into every decision, to the point where I'm not convinced this remake has taken any less time and effort than an all-new Zelda game," he said.
"Ocarina of Time is obviously one of the great video game experiences in the history of the medium, but I have no doubt this new version will be the best way to experience this story.
"It's fleshed out as a world, sumptuously detailed, and the controls match 21st-Century expectations."
Ed King, known as Zeltik to his 893,000 followers on YouTube, said "the level of detail and charm" in the Ocarina of Time remake stood out.

"The Forest Temple has always been my favourite Zelda dungeon: a mysterious, haunted mansion in the deep woods, a lost work of man slowly being reclaimed by nature," he said. "The remake really leans into the surreal, uncanny nature of the original dungeon."
And fellow YouTuber StrawHatMidas said it was the "perfect" way to "bring this classic back".

"Not only does the game pay homage to the Nintendo 64 original, but it also expands on the things that made it so memorable," he said. "Everything from the world and atmosphere to the controls and soundtrack feels like a love letter to the classic Zelda formula."
Has Nintendo played it too safe?
Nintendo has made some big changes, not least to the Water Temple - a dungeon about two thirds into the game.
Aonuma said, having worked on the original, this was what he personally wanted to change most due to its reputation for being "very, very difficult".

He said there was now "a greater facility in tackling" the dungeon, as players can now easily change a critical in-game item known as heavy boots and have "the ability to leverage the camera orientation".
I grew up playing Zelda on the N64, which pioneered the joystick - but nowadays two sticks is the standard, with one to move and one to control the camera.
As far as I'm concerned, being able to freely move the camera this time round was a significant improvement.

At times, the trip down memory lane was captivating. I knew where to go and what to do, thanks to a kind of muscle memory. However, on occasion that took away from the experience - with some tasks achieved too easily and some puzzles too quickly because I recalled their solutions.
Some people will love how similar it is, but I have to wonder if Nintendo has played things a bit too safe.
I don't think the developers see it that way.
"Even if the game may look different, we've maintained the essence that the original developers wanted to and hopefully conveyed through the original Ocarina of Time," Fujibayashi said.
Don't get me wrong - the game has lots of changes and surprises, and I won't spoil them, but I wish there had been more.
Then again, perhaps the best games leave you wanting more.
Or as Mike put it: "I loved the original as much as the next person, but I don't think I'll be going back to it."
Fans will no doubt wonder whether this is it, or if there will be more Zelda on the horizon. With the franchise's first movie coming next year, there's certainly more to come in the short term.
And in the long term, I wondered if with 30 more years of technological advancements, Nintendo might consider remaking the game once again.
"I will be long retired," Aonuma said, with a laugh.

articles.headline: Trump says he asked Dana White, UFC boss, to be his new White House press secretary
keyFacts: Donald Trump announced on social media that he offered UFC chief executive Dana White the job of White House press secretary.
The White House press secretary position has been vacant for three weeks after former appointee Katie Zacharia was forced to resign.
White said he is traveling to Washington to meet with Trump on Monday, without stating whether he will accept the role.
body: Donald Trump has offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, the president said in a social media post on Saturday.

Trump described White, who staged a cage-fighting spectacle at the White House to mark the president’s 80th birthday in June, as “a violent Fighter and Warrior”, credentials unlike any ever used to describe previous press secretaries.

Trump added that he asked White, a vocal supporter who campaigned for him in 2024, to bring six UFC fighters with him to serve as press aides. “We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote. “Dana, please take the job!”

It was initially unclear whether the job offer was part of an actual plan, or an attention-grabbing stunt from a president desperate to change the subject from the huge losses suffered by his party in elections this week.

There was no immediate response from White, who, some observers noted, might hesitate to leave a lucrative role running the UFC, which has earned him a fortune estimated to be in excess of $600m, for a job in government service that pays $195,000 a year.

Later on Saturday, after CNN reported that White had declined the offer and that one aide to the president had described it as a joke, White posted an Instagram story with an image of himself in the White House briefing room above the caption: “On to the next chapter.”

The UFC boss was then asked about the president’s post at a news conference after a boxing match in London on Saturday night. “I’m flying to Washington DC right now” to meet with Trump, White replied, without saying whether he would accept the job. “I’m going to meet with him, we have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that,” he added.

The president’s Truth Social post was illustrated by seven images, including what appeared to be an AI-generated image of White behind the presidential seal in a press room, and photographs of the six UFC fighters whom Trump fantasizes about deploying to deal with reporters who ask him awkward questions: Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov (who are both from a Muslim-majority region of Russia), Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harrison – whose last name was mistakenly rendered as “Harris” by the president.

In his post, Trump acknowledged that two of his dream hires, Makhachev and Nurmagomedov, are not Americans, but he did not mention that Nurmagomedov is reportedly close to the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, or that Makhachev has spoken out in defense of Palestinian civilians killed by Israel in Gaza. In 2023, Makhachev also celebrated a victory in one fight by saying, “Alhamdulillah,” the Arabic phrase for “praise be to God” used by Muslims. Democrat Abdul El-Sayed was criticized in the rightwing media for using that same Arabic phrase in his victory speech this week.

The first in a series of taxpayer-funded pro-Trump ads broadcast by the White House in the run-up to the recent midterms closed with images of the UFC fight on Trump’s birthday and remarks about him from White, who could be heard saying: “He is the toughest, most resilient human being I have ever met in my life.” White used that formulation to describe Trump multiple times during the 2024 presidential election campaign, most notably to sing Trump’s praises at the Republican national convention.

The role of White House press secretary has been vacant for three weeks, since Trump’s previous pick, far-right commentator Katie Zacharia, was forced to resign after trying, and failing, to dodge questions about why she described herself as an attorney despite having failed the bar exam.
Henry Smith contributed reporting

articles.headline: LEGO Black Friday 2026 Sales: What to Expect
keyFacts: Black Friday sales offer discounts of 30%, 40%, or up to 50% off on various LEGO sets.
Retailers are expected to discount retiring sets to clear inventory for upcoming new releases.
The 5,363-piece LEGO Godzilla set launches for $449.99 on November 27 at 12:01 a.m.
body: On nearly every IGN article about LEGO sets (and as the LEGO editor here at IGN, I post a lot of them), commenters complain that LEGO sets cost too much. That’s a fair criticism, especially because many of the most noteworthy LEGO sets are expensive .

Even the smaller sets cost more than you might expect if you don’t pay attention to the market. They’re comprised of many tiny interlocking pieces, after all. If you feel like you’re priced out of many LEGO sets you’d want to buy, Black Friday offers an excellent opportunity to buy them at some of the lowest prices of the year.
The question is, what kinds of discounts on LEGO can we expect to see this Black Friday? I’ve been covering LEGO deals for many years now, so here’s what I expect based on my experience.
LEGO Sets Up to 50% Off

Many times throughout the year, LEGO sets go on sale at various retailers. These run-of-the-mill sales generally offer discounts of 20% off. That’s the standard sale price at retailers like Amazon, Target, Best Buy, and the LEGO Store.
Therefore, a particularly good sale on LEGO sets is when you can find them for 30%, 40%, or even 50% off . These are the kinds of discounts I expect to see once the true Black Friday sales begin.
LEGO Store's Black Friday Sale

Unlike many retailers, the official LEGO Store tends to have a pretty short-lived Black Friday sale. Last year's sale started on Black Friday and ran for fours days – which means through that weekend and Cyber Monday. But the LEGO Store won't be the only retailer dropping prices on LEGO sets, so keep an eye on the Black Friday sale schedule to see when retailers like Amazon and Walmart's sales will go live.
Discounts on Retiring Sets
Which brings us to the question of which sets are most likely to be discounted? Answer: the sets that are retiring soon.

LEGO releases hundreds of new sets each year ( here’s our running tally of the 2026 releases ). To make room on retailer shelves for all those new boxes, LEGO has to retires older sets at roughly the same rate. Right now, LEGO’s “retiring soon” page has over 200 sets on it. You can bet many of these will go on sale during Black Friday as retailers try to offload inventory to make way for upcoming LEGO sets .
Black Friday LEGO Godzilla Set
Each year, LEGO releases a major new set on Black Friday. It’s always a statement piece, and it’s priced accordingly.

This year’s Black Friday set is LEGO Godzilla , a towering 5,363-piece set that stands over two feet tall. It features a striking gray-and-blue version of the city-wrecker that looks menacing and highly detailed. I love it. It will be available for $449.99, starting at 12:01 a.m. November 27.

If you buy it between November 27 - 30 while supplies last, you’ll also get an additional LEGO set as a free Gift With Purchase. It’s LEGO Godzilla Logo & Footprint , and it’s meant to be displayed next to the King of Monsters. It has matching colors and looks phenomenal.
LEGO Insiders Weekend 2026

Every year on the weekend before Black Friday, LEGO runs an “Insiders Weekend” promotion. This is a LEGO Store sale that’s exclusive to LEGO Insiders, a free membership that gets you access to events like this ( you can sign up here ). In addition to discounts on select sets, it also gets you things like bonus loyalty points on purchases, as well as exclusive Gifts with Purchase. You can check out last year’s promotions for an idea of what promotions we might expect to see in 2026.

articles.headline: Denzel Bentley trades words with Conor Benn over fight after beating Shane Mosley Jr
keyFacts: Denzel Bentley secured a unanimous decision victory over Shane Mosley Jr at the Copper Box.
Bentley and Conor Benn exchanged words ringside regarding a potential future fight between the two boxers.
Benn responded to Bentley's challenge by stating the bout would be easy work any day of the week.
body: Denzel Bentley and Conor Benn traded words over a potential 2027 showdown after the former’s win over Shane Mosley Jr.
Bentley was making his debut under Dana White ‘s Zuffa Boxing banner.
Bentley scored an impressive win against Mosley Jr, before taking aim at another son of a boxing icon in Benn Getty
There were distractions outside of the ring for the British middleweight, who was stripped of his WBO world title once he signed to face Mosley Jr.
Nonetheless he went ahead with his plans to face the son of the boxing legend and Hall of Famer Mosley, and was looking for a statement win.
Bentley made a fantastic start dropping the American in the second round, but was unable to force a stoppage.
However, he did continue to control the vast majority of the contest, and scored an impressive unanimous decision victory.
The scorecards read at 96-94, 96-93 and 95-94 across the ten rounds, and gave Bentley a much deserved win in front of the Copper Box crowd.
It was a decent scalp for ‘2 Sharp’ with Mosley Jr on the back of a solid victory over Serhii Bohachuk 5 months ago.
Bentley trades words with Benn after win
Focus naturally after the impressive win was on what was next for the recent world champion.
He suggested there were multiple options on the table given his prominence in the rankings.
But his main choice was a potential all-British clash with Benn, who sat ringside.
He shouted: “I’d love a world title shot, but if it’s not one of the champions, there’s another middleweight sat right there.
View Tweet: https://t.co/58gY5Wv0St
‘The Destroyer’ beamed on at the hearing of his name, and quickly responded.
“Easy work,” he quipped back. “Any day of the week.”
Benn hasn’t fought since losing to Ryan Garcia in his own world title shot, although he has started entertaining talks of a 2027 return.
And a showdown with Bentley would likely be realistic given they are under the same promotional stable.
After defeat to Garcia , Benn’s plan is also to move to at least the 160lbs division where he famously beat Chris Eubank Jr in their rematch.
So a clash between the pair would make perfect sense, but would represent a stern test for the Essex star name.

articles.headline: Can Verstappen, Hamilton come from the back in Sao Paulo 'reverse grid' race?
keyFacts: Lando Norris starts on pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix alongside new world champion Kimi Antonelli.
Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start at the back of the grid due to power unit changes.
The race takes place on Sunday at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, with a high chance of rain forecast.
body: Sao Paulo GP: Can Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton come from the back again as Lando Norris hopes for rain to fight Kimi Antonelli

Lando Norris starts on pole in Brazil from Kimi Antonelli but there will be plenty of attention further down the field with Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton starting at the back; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm
Saturday 7 November 2026 23:26, UK
A mixed up grid and rain on the forecast has set up the prospect of a thrilling Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Sunday.
For the third year in a row, Lando Norris will start on pole position in Brazil with new F1 world champion Kimi Antonelli alongside him on the front row.

Unusually though, there will be plenty of attention further down the field as power unit changes for Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton mean they start at the back, while Ferrari's Charles Leclerc starts 14th for a 10-grid place penalty.
- How Mercedes can win Constructors' Championship this Sunday
